question: Should OpenClaw support config-backed SecretRefs for Docker sandbox environment variables even though their resolved values remain observable through Docker container and daemon metadata?
rationale: The implementation follows existing SecretRef and Docker-env patterns, but it deliberately creates a new supported route from secret stores into a container-visible environment boundary; that acceptance is product and security policy, not a mechanical code decision.

options.title: Approve the scoped SecretRef extension
options.body: Accept the documented Docker metadata exposure boundary, require a current-main rebase and refreshed focused validation, then continue normal merge review.

options.title: Keep Docker sandbox env literal-only
options.body: Reject this credential materialization surface and close the implementation path while retaining the existing literal environment configuration behavior.

options.title: Pause for a safer sandbox secret-delivery design
options.body: Defer this PR until maintainers define a delivery mechanism that avoids exposing resolved credentials through Docker environment metadata.

recommendation.title: Approve the scoped SecretRef extension
recommendation.body: Accept the documented Docker metadata exposure boundary, require a current-main rebase and refreshed focused validation, then continue normal merge review.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged work owns both the Docker sandbox environment path and the runtime SecretRef-resolution pattern this decision combines.
